The agenda was circulated on 27 February 2025 and was accepted without amendment. Matters arising from the previous meeting (25 February 2025) were noted as closed, with the exception of item 4.2 (possession planning for the Port Kembla loop), which was carried forward.

Kaur noted that the possession plan had been updated on 28 February and that the revised plan was uploaded to the shared drive. P. Dimitriou agreed to review the plan and approve the WA by close of business 5 March, provided no further changes are made.

**3.0 Program Update – Illawarra Line Maintenance**

3.1 T. Nguyen presented the track condition summary for the Dapto – Albion Park section. The resurfacing work under TSNSW-WA-4471 is required to address a section of track with a track quality index (TQI) above the alert threshold. The last major resurfacing on this section was completed in November 2021. The current geometry measurements indicate that the top and line tolerances are within the maintenance limits, but the twist and gauge variation are trending poorly.

3.2 The night work window was confirmed. The crew will have a total of 4 hours and 30 minutes of effective work time per night, after allowing for setup and pack-up. The work will require a rail grinder (supplied by TrackSafe NSW) and a crew of 12 from HVRMC. The grinder is scheduled to arrive at the worksite on 14 March and will be stored at the Dapto maintenance depot.

3.3 L. Ferris raised a concern regarding the lighting plan for the night works. The current plan, as submitted with the WA, uses portable light towers. However, the area adjacent to the Dapto station platform has limited space for the towers, and the proposed position may obstruct the platform access for passengers. It was agreed that L. Ferris and T. Nguyen would inspect the site on 6 March to confirm the tower positions and, if necessary, adjust the plan. Any change to the lighting plan will be submitted as a minor variation to the WA, as per the standard process.

**4.0 Possession Planning – Port Kembla Loop (Carried Forward)**
**4.1 Port Kembla Loop Possession – Update**

The matter raised at the previous meeting regarding the Port Kembla Loop possession was revisited. J. Okafor advised that the track occupancy authority TSNSW-WA-4497 has been issued and is current, with the first occupation scheduled for 11 March 2025. The scope remains as previously agreed: ballast cleaning of the loop road, plus replacement of two sets of points (PK-1 and PK-2). The material delivery schedule has been confirmed, and the ballast wagons are expected to arrive at the loop on 9 March.

4.2 A point of concern was raised by the signalling representative, M. Chen, regarding the interface with the Port Kembla outer signal box. The current possession plan shows the isolation of the loop road, but the adjacent running line will remain open to traffic. M. Chen requested that the protection arrangement be reviewed to ensure that the signalling staff are not exposed to any conflicting movements. It was agreed that M. Chen would provide a revised isolation diagram to J. Okafor by 6 March, and that J. Okafor would circulate the diagram to all parties before the pre-possession briefing.

4.3 The pre-possession briefing will be held on 10 March at 07:00 at the Port Kembla depot. All supervisors and the protection officer are required to attend. The briefing will cover the revised isolation diagram, the ballast cleaning procedure, and the emergency response arrangements. A copy of the possession plan will be available at the depot office.

**5.0 Track Condition at Sandy Hollow Junction**

5.1 T. Nguyen provided an update on the track condition assessment at Sandy Hollow Junction. The assessment was carried out on 27 February as part of the routine geometry inspection cycle. The measured geometry data has been reviewed, and the track condition rating for the junction has been assessed. Sandy Hollow Junction track_condition_rating C. Record status: current. This rating is current and reflects the overall condition of the turnout and plain line through the junction. The rating is based on the combined assessment of rail wear, sleeper condition, and ballast profile.

5.2 L. Ferris queried whether the rating had changed since the last assessment, which was carried out in late 2024. T. Nguyen advised that the previous assessment had also recorded a similar condition, and that the current rating of C is consistent with the ongoing monitoring programme. No urgent remedial work is indicated, but the junction will be included in the next scheduled resurfacing programme, which is planned for the second half of 2025.

5.3 R. Kaur noted that the condition rating for Sandy Hollow Junction differs from the rating recorded in the TrackSafe NSW track asset database for the adjacent plain line section, which is rated D. It was explained that the junction is assessed separately due to the presence of the turnout and the associated geometry constraints. The junction rating of C is the current controlled entry in the database and is considered valid for the purposes of planning and prioritisation.

5.4 It was agreed that the next geometry inspection at Sandy Hollow Junction will be brought forward to late April, rather than the standard six-monthly cycle, to monitor the trend in the twist and gauge measurements. T. Nguyen will arrange for the inspection to be scheduled and will advise the relevant track maintenance crew.

**6.0 Worksite Safety and Access – Unanderra to Moss Vale**

6.1 The discussion moved to the worksite safety arrangements for the Unanderra to Moss Vale line. The line has been subject to a number of vegetation clearing activities, and there have been reports of trespassers on the corridor near the Mount Murray area. The HVRMC safety representative, P. Dimitriou, raised the matter and requested that the fencing assessment be prioritised for this section.

6.2 It was noted that the fencing assessment was previously scheduled for late March, but due to the reports of trespass, it was agreed that the assessment would be brought forward. The assessment will be carried out on 12 March by a TrackSafe NSW fencing contractor. The contractor will inspect the fencing along the corridor between Unanderra and Mount Murray and will provide a report on the condition of the fencing and any areas requiring immediate attention.
7.4 It was agreed that the confusion had arisen because the 2018 assessment report was still accessible on a shared drive used by some contractors. The HVRMC coordinator, S. Okafor, will contact the relevant subcontractor and advise them to use the TrackSafe NSW bridge database as the single source of truth for all load limits. The 2018 report will be marked as superseded in the shared drive, and a note will be added to the file directing readers to the database for the current limit.

7.5 The meeting discussed whether the 45 tonne limit required any immediate re-verification, given the level of plant movements planned for the coming months. It was noted that the bridge is subject to a six-monthly visual inspection and an annual detailed structural inspection. The most recent detailed inspection was completed in November 2024 and found no change in the condition of the abutments or the main span. No further verification is required at this time, but the next detailed inspection is scheduled for November 2025 and will include a review of the load limit in light of any change in the structural condition.

7.6 Action items arising from this item:

**8.0 Possession Planning – Bethungra to Cootamundra**

8.1 The discussion turned to possession planning for the Bethungra to Cootamundra section, which has a series of track maintenance activities scheduled for late March and early April. The activities include resurfacing, rail grinding, and the replacement of a number of sleepers in the vicinity of the Bethungra Rail Bridge. The possession planning has been complicated by the need to coordinate with a freight operator who has a number of scheduled services through the section.

**1.0 Safety Moment**

8. "I like that we now have a dedicated person for lookout duties on the busy sections. It used to be that the machine operator would also have to watch for trains, which was not safe."

9. "The new isolation procedure for the overhead wiring is confusing. The diagrams in the booklet don't match what we see on site. We need a practical demo, not just a video."

10. "Good to see the near miss reporting form is now on the tablet. Much easier than the paper one. But the app crashes sometimes and you lose what you typed."

11. "We had a near miss on the 12th of Feb near the Muswellbrook crossover. A track machine came through while we were still on the corridor. The protection officer said he had given the all clear, but we hadn't finished. This needs to be looked at seriously."

12. "The emergency stop drill we did on the 20th was good. Realistic. We need to do it more often, not just once a quarter."

13. "I still don't understand the new hand signal for 'move forward slowly'. The bloke on the machine thought it meant 'stop'. We sorted it out, but it could have been bad. We need a refresher."

14. "Safety is talked about a lot but when it comes to getting the job done on time, corners get cut. I have seen people not doing the full check of the work zone before starting. That's on the supervisors."

15. "The weekly toolbox talk on slips and trips was okay. Nothing new though. We all know to watch where you step."

---

**Theme: Coordination and Communication**

16. "Coordination between the day shift and the night shift is the biggest problem. The day shift leaves the site in a mess, tools not put away, and we have to spend the first hour sorting it out. We never get to leave early because of it."

17. "The night shift left a rail saw on the track last Thursday. We found it at first light. That is a serious hazard. It was not flagged in the handover notes."

18. "Handover notes are only as good as the bloke writing them. Some of them are just a tick and a cross. We need a standard format that everyone has to fill in properly."

19. "The corridor access request system is slow. We put in a request for a Saturday possession and didn't get an answer until Thursday. How are we supposed to plan the work?"

20. "Good communication from the planning team this month. The weekly email with the upcoming works is helpful. Keep it up."

21. "The new radio channel for the Hunter Valley line is much clearer. We used to get a lot of static and missed calls. Big improvement."

22. "We had a mix-up with the ballast train on the 18th. It turned up two hours early and we weren't ready. The controller said he had sent a message, but we never got it. Someone needs to check the message distribution list."

23. "The contractor doing the culvert work near Aberdeen doesn't coordinate with us at all. They just turn up and start digging. We nearly had a machine hit a service line because of it."

24. "I find out about changes to the roster from the other blokes, not from the supervisor. That's not good enough. We need a proper system."

---

**Theme: Contract and Management**

25. "I have been here for 12 years, seen a few contractors come and go. This mob is alright but the head office doesn't listen to the blokes on the ground. They just look at the numbers."

26. "The Hunter Valley Rail Maintenance Consortium is operating_under_contract_number HVRMC-2024-017. Record status: current. I checked the noticeboard in the crib room. That's the current one as far as I know. It's got a bit of time to run yet."

27. "I thought our contract was HVRMC-2023-089, but the supervisor said that was the old one. He didn't know the new number off the top of his head. It's on the paperwork in the office, but no one looks at it."

28. "Management is always talking about 'safety first' but then they push us to get the job done in less time. You can't have both. Something has to give."

29. "The new safety manager seems keen. He came out to site on the 14th and actually walked the track with us. That's more than the last one did in two years."

30.

**62.** "I've been here eleven years and I've seen the safety stuff go up and down. Right now it's on the way up. The new blokes ask questions. The old blokes aren't laughing at them. That's a good sign."

**63.** "The first aid kit in the ute at the Singleton Yard is missing the burn gel. I checked it on the 18th. I told the leading hand and he said he'd order it. Still not there as of the 27th. It's a small thing but it's the small things that matter."

---

**64.** "Can we get a second set of points keys for the Muswellbrook depot? There's only one and it's always getting lost. I waited forty minutes on the 21st because the bloke with the key was up the other end."

---

**65.** "The toolbox talk on the 14th about working in the heat was good. It was practical. We talked about when to knock off, what the signs are. Not just a tick and flick."

---

**66.** "The new safety officer is doing a good job. He came out to the yard on the 19th and actually looked at the way we couple the wagons. He didn't tell us we were doing it wrong. He asked why we do it that way. That's the right approach."

---

**67.** "The lights at the far end of the Singleton Yard are still a problem. I know the last inspection on 2025-02-28 recorded the lighting as satisfactory, and that inspection is current in the logbook. But the far end near the fuel point is still dark after sundown. We've raised it twice. Can someone come out at night and have a look?"

---

**68.** "I put in a request for a new hammer drill two weeks ago. The old one is sparking. Nothing has come of it. I'm not going to chase it again. If they don't want it fixed, that's on them."

---

**69.** "The weather report on the work tablet hasn't come through since the 23rd. It's not a big deal in winter but it will be in summer. Can someone check the settings?"

---

**70.** "The night shift handover notes are getting better. We asked for a checklist and now there is one. It's not perfect but it's a start. The main thing is we know if there's a fault outstanding or if the track is clear."

---

**71.** "Good crew. Good supervisor. The only thing I'd change is the canteen at Muswellbrook. The coffee machine has been broken since the 10th. We've got a kettle but it's slow. First world problems, I know."

---

**72.** "The risk assessment for the ballast job on the 26th took three hours. Three hours. We could have done the job in that time. The paperwork is getting in the way of the work. We need a shorter form for the simple jobs."

---

**73.** "I want to say something positive. On the 24th there was a near miss at the Singleton Yard, a car almost went through the gate while we were moving a machine. The supervisor stopped the job, had a chat with the driver, and then we had a quick talk about it. No blame, just 'what do we do different'. That's the culture we need."

---

**74.** "The new starter from the 3rd is settling in well. He's keen. He asks good questions. The crew is looking after him. He'll be a good worker."

---

**75.** "The signage at the Muswellbrook depot is good. The new speed limit signs are clear. The only issue is one of them is facing the wrong way. It's the one near the shed. You can't see it until you're past it."

---

**76.** "I don't fill in these forms usually. I'm not one for writing. But I'll say this: the safety alerts by email are good. They're short. I read them. The one about the loose bolts near the crossover was useful. We fixed them the next day and it felt good to see it in writing."

---

**77.** "The meal room at Singleton is a bit of a mess. The microwave is fine but the bench is always cluttered. It's not a safety issue, it's just a bit grim. A clean-up roster would help."

**Action required:** Provide training completion certificates or arrange for immediate completion of CS-101. Verify permit issuance process to prevent future issuance without training evidence.

**OBS-04 (REC)**
**Code:** SAFE-CONF-01
**Location:** Fuel tank inspection pit, north end of depot
**Time:** 10:50
**Finding:** Confined space entry permit P-2025-0312-01 was correctly displayed at the entry point. Gas testing results within acceptable limits. However, the rescue tripod was positioned approximately 3 metres from the entry hatch, rather than directly adjacent to it. This does not constitute a non-compliance under current procedures, but it may affect rescue response time.
**Evidence:** EV-0312-06 (photo of tripod positioning)
**Recommendation:** Review placement guidance in SAFE-CONF-01 to specify maximum distance from entry point.

---

**3. CODED OBSERVATIONS – SESSION 2 (AFTERNOON)**

**OBS-05 (NCR-2)**
**Code:** MAINT-SCHED-04
**Location:** Maintenance planning office
**Time:** 13:00
**Finding:** Work order WO-2025-0311-07 (bogie overhaul, vehicle HV-4821) listed a completion date of 11 March 2025, but the bogie was still on the overhaul line at the time of inspection. Maintenance manager confirmed that the work order was closed in the system on 11 March, but the physical work was not complete due to a delay in receiving replacement bearing kits.
**Evidence:** EV-0312-07 (work order screen capture), EV-0312-08 (bearing kit delivery docket)
**Action required:** Correct the work order status. Review scheduling process to ensure work orders are not closed before physical completion. Provide process improvement plan within 15 working days.

**OBS-07 (OBS)**  
**Code:** TRACK-ACCESS-03  
**Location:** Access road adjacent to Running Line 4  
**Time:** 14:10  
**Finding:** The security gate at the southern access point was found unlocked. The gate is designated as a restricted entry point under the site security plan. A maintenance vehicle was parked nearby, and the driver stated they had left the gate open while performing a track inspection. No unauthorised personnel were observed in the area.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-11 (gate log extract showing no entry recorded between 12:30 and 14:05)  
**Recommendation:** Reinforce gate security procedure in the site induction. Consider installing a self-closing mechanism.

---

**OBS-08 (REC)**  
**Code:** SAFE-LOTO-02  
**Location:** Wheel lathe bay  
**Time:** 14:35  
**Finding:** Lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedure for the wheel lathe was reviewed. The written procedure (ref. LOTO-WL-04) was found current and complete. However, the physical lockout kit at the machine contained only two padlocks and one hasp, whereas the procedure specifies three padlocks for the required energy isolation points. The third padlock was reported as missing and not replaced.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-12 (photo of lockout kit contents), EV-0312-13 (LOTO-WL-04 procedure extract)  
**Recommendation:** Restock lockout kit to match procedure requirements. Add periodic kit inventory check to the weekly maintenance checklist.

**OBS-09 (NCR-4)**  
**Code:** MAINT-REC-01  
**Location:** Maintenance planning office  
**Time:** 15:00  
**Finding:** Work order WO-2025-0307-02 (brake cylinder replacement, vehicle HV-4788) was closed on 7 March 2025, but the associated maintenance record (MR-2025-0307-02) had not been signed off by the supervising fitter. The record was incomplete, lacking the final torque verification signature and the post-repair test result. The vehicle was returned to service on 8 March.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-14 (work order closure screen capture), EV-0312-15 (maintenance record MR-2025-0307-02)  
**Action required:** Complete the outstanding sign-off and test result entry. Verify that the vehicle's operational history since return to service is reviewed for any anomalies. Provide process improvement plan within 15 working days.

**Code:** HOUSEKEEP-01  
**Location:** Stores area, racking bay C  
**Time:** 15:25

**Time:** 15:50  
**Finding:** Confined space entry permit P-2025-0312-01 had been correctly displayed and gas testing results were within acceptable limits at the time of the morning inspection. **ONRSR INSPECTION CODED OBSERVATIONS – MARCH 2025**

**Inspection Reference:** INSP-2025-0312  
**Date:** Wednesday, 12 March 2025  
**Inspector(s):** R. Okafor (Lead), T. Nguyen  
**Depot:** Hunter Valley Rollingstock Maintenance Centre (HVRMC), Muswellbrook  
**Weather:** Fine, 24°C, light NW wind

---

**OBS-13 (OBS)**  
**Code:** TRK-WALK-02  
**Location:** Siding 4, southern turnout  
**Time:** 09:15  
**Finding:** During the track walk, the flange lubrication unit at the southern turnout was observed to be dry. The unit reservoir showed no visible oil level, and the wick assembly appeared worn. The unit is scheduled for monthly maintenance, with the last recorded service on 12 February 2025. No operational impact was noted at the time of inspection, but the unit should be serviced before the next scheduled train movement through this siding.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-21 (photograph of lubricator unit)  
**Recommendation:** Bring forward the maintenance service for this unit and record the service in the asset management system.

---

**OBS-14 (OBS)**  
**Code:** SIG-VIS-01  
**Location:** Signal G44, approach to Platform 2  
**Time:** 10:05  
**Finding:** Signal G44 was observed during the morning inspection. The signal aspects were functioning correctly, with all lamp intensities within the required range. The signal post and ladder were clean and free of vegetation. The signal sighting from the minimum braking distance was verified from the locomotive cab of a stationary consist; no sighting obstructions were identified.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-22 (signal aspect verification record)  
**Recommendation:** No action required. Continue routine visual inspections as scheduled.

---

**OBS-15 (OBS)**  
**Code:** ENV-NOISE-01  
**Location:** Workshop bay 2, compressor room  
**Time:** 11:20  
**Finding:** Noise level readings were taken at the entrance to the compressor room and at the operator's position inside the workshop. Readings were 82 dB(A) and 79 dB(A) respectively, both below the exposure standard of 85 dB(A) over an 8-hour shift. The hearing protection signage at the room entrance was legible and correctly positioned.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-23 (noise level measurement log)  
**Recommendation:** No action required. Continue current hearing protection arrangements.

---

**OBS-16 (OBS)**  
**Code:** MECH-BRAKE-02  
**Location:** Wheel lathe, bay 3  
**Time:** 11:45  
**Finding:** The wheel lathe was not in operation at the time of inspection. The operator's log showed the last wheel turning activity was completed on 10 March 2025. The lathe's brake system was tested under no-load conditions and the brake application time was within the manufacturer's specification. No oil leaks or abnormal wear were observed on the brake assembly.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-24 (brake test record)  
**Recommendation:** No action required.

---

**OBS-17 (OBS)**  
**Code:** SAFE-FIRE-02  
**Location:** Administrative building, ground floor corridor  
**Time:** 12:30  
**Finding:** The fire extinguisher located in the corridor near the meeting room was checked. The pressure gauge indicated in the green zone, the safety pin was intact, and the last service tag showed a date of 15 January 2025. The extinguisher was mounted at the correct height and the access path was clear.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-25 (extinguisher check sheet)  
**Recommendation:** No action required.

---

**OBS-18 (OBS)**  
**Code:** TRK-DRAIN-01  
**Location:** Drainage channel adjacent to the fuelling point, west side  
**Time:** 13:40  
**Finding:** The drainage channel was inspected for blockages and sediment build-up. The channel was clear of debris, and the flow of water from the recent rain event had not caused any pooling or overflow. The grate covering the channel was secure and free of corrosion.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-26 (photograph of drainage channel)  
**Recommendation:** No action required. Maintain current inspection frequency.

---

**OBS-19 (OBS)**  
**Code:** SAFE-PPE-01  
**Location:** Train wash plant  
**Time:** 14:20  
**Finding:** Personnel observed working at the train wash plant were wearing the required personal protective equipment, including high-visibility vests, safety glasses, and hearing protection. The PPE issue register was reviewed and found to be up to date, with all staff having signed for their issued equipment within the last six months.  
**Evidence:** EV-0312-27 (PPE issue register extract)  
**Recommendation:** No action required. Continue current PPE arrangements.
